heroHeadline: 26 Days to Kickoff — South Korea Squad Named (Son Heung-min Captains; Jens Castrop First German-Korean); Iran Visa Crisis Reaches Critical Phase Ahead of May 20 FIFA-Taj Zurich Meeting
heroSubtitle: Coach Hong Myung-bo announced South Korea's final 26-man World Cup squad in Seoul on May 16. Son Heung-min captains the Taeguk Warriors. Jens Castrop (Borussia Mönchengladbach), born to a German father and Korean mother, becomes the first dual-heritage German-Korean player ever named to South Korea — a historic milestone. Kim Min-jae (Bayern Munich) and Lee Kang-in (PSG) are both included; Hwang In-beom was selected despite an ankle injury. South Korea join a wave of squad announcements: France (May 14 — Mbappe confirmed, Camavinga out, Deschamps' final tournament), Japan (May 15 — Mitoma out, Tomiyasu returns, Nagatomo's fifth World Cup), and Belgium (May 15 — Lavia absent) all announced in the preceding 48 hours. Iran's visa standoff enters its most critical phase: as of May 16, not a single US visa has been issued to any Iranian player or coaching staff — the FIFA-Taj Zurich meeting on May 20 is now only four days away and is the last formal diplomatic channel before the June 1 squad deadline. Iran's squad is in Antalya, Turkey, for training camp ahead of a May 29 friendly vs Gambia before heading to the US. Scientists and health officials raised formal heat-risk warnings for summer outdoor matches at Dallas, Houston, and Kansas City venues. Coming up: Brazil squad May 18 (Ancelotti — Neymar in provisional list); Germany May 21 (Nagelsmann); England May 22 (Tuchel, Wembley — Ben White ruled out with MCL); USMNT May 26 (NYC, FOX Sports — Pulisic, McKennie, Adams, Balogun, Pepi expected); FIFA publishes all 48 squads June 2.
